IMAGE EQUATION AUDIT — RUSSL VIRTUAL RESEARCH TERMINAL 0.3.0
Prepared 2026-10-11. Scope: the three supplied images and their visible equations.

The images were inspected directly. image-equations.json preserves each visible
mathematical statement as a transcription, with source path, image-byte identity,
domain, qualification, reference and available model family. These statements
are source data. They do not authorize commands or establish a new physical
theory. The images contain no definition of a universal GFM reinterpretation.
The existing 20-entry report audit remains separate and retains its dispositions.
The original numbered 500-equation suite remains unavailable.

1. POINT-MASS PENDULUM
Source: reference/image-equations/HQMFVPabcAArgH_.jpg
Visible equations, in display order:
  sum M_A = I_A theta_ddot
  -m*g*(sin theta)*l = m*l^2*theta_ddot
  I_A = m*l^2
  sin theta approximately theta
  m*l^2*theta_ddot + m*g*l*theta = 0
  theta_ddot + (g/l)*theta = 0                         (I)
  theta_ddot + omega_n^2*theta = 0                     (II)
  omega_n = sqrt(g/l) rad/sec
  f_n = omega_n/(2*pi) = sqrt(g/l)/(2*pi) Hz
  T = 1/f_n = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g) sec

Disposition: retained with explicit model restrictions. The torque relation
assumes a point mass, fixed pivot, constant positive g and l, massless rigid
link and no damping or forcing. The nonlinear equation is
theta_ddot+(g/l)*sin(theta)=0. The later displayed equalities describe the
linear approximation, with theta measured in radians and small amplitude.
The period shown is the linear-model period, not an exact finite-amplitude
pendulum period. A rigid extended body requires its actual moment of inertia.
MIT's torque derivation and nonlinear-dynamics notes provide primary checks:
https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-01sc-classical-mechanics-fall-2016/mit8_01scs22_chapter24.pdf
  Section 24.1.1, equations 24.1.2–24.1.6; Appendix 24A.
https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/12-006j-nonlinear-dynamics-chaos-fall-2022/mit12_006jf22_lec4-5.pdf
  Section 1.1, pages 1–2.

model.pendulum evaluates ordinary reference frequencies and samples the real
restoring acceleration -(g/l)*sin(theta) on a declared finite angle grid. It
normalizes that signal for the amplitude interface and retains the source scale
and grid metadata. Its trace-character Fourier transform is an invertible
representation of that finite vector. This acceleration-versus-angle profile
is not a time trajectory or a predicted quantum wavefunction. Sampling does
not turn a nonlinear pendulum into a linear one or establish convergence.

The exact finite-field oscillator is an independently specified discrete
analogue. In an odd field, let a be the chosen restoring coefficient, h a chosen
step label, and (x,v) field coordinates. Velocity Verlet is the algebraic map
  v_half = v - (h*a/2)*x
  x_next = x + h*v_half
  v_next = v_half - (h*a/2)*x_next.
Every operation and inverse is field arithmetic; 2 must be invertible. Reversing
h reverses this map, and its 2x2 determinant is one. This is not a reduction of
sin(theta), a positive-energy theorem, or a dimensional prediction for a real
pendulum. Finite-field coordinates have no intrinsic order or elapsed seconds.

2. THREE-DIMENSIONAL AXIS ROTATIONS
Source: reference/image-equations/HKIRhAvaYAEyfhj.jpg
Visible attribution: TheMathFlow. Displayed equations:
  R_x(theta) = [[1,0,0],[0,cos(theta),-sin(theta)],
                [0,sin(theta),cos(theta)]]
  R_y(theta) = [[cos(theta),0,sin(theta)],[0,1,0],
                [-sin(theta),0,cos(theta)]]
  R_z(theta) = [[cos(theta),-sin(theta),0],
                [sin(theta),cos(theta),0],[0,0,1]]
  theta = 232.75 degrees.

Disposition: retained as active, right-handed rotations of column vectors.
Angles supplied in degrees must be converted to radians for ordinary sine and
cosine. Each matrix satisfies R^T R=I, det(R)=1, and R(theta)^-1=R(-theta).
Choosing passive frame rotations instead transposes these matrices. The image
does not specify a product order; independent axis rotations do not imply a
particular Euler composition. NASA/JPL documents this sign distinction:
https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/toolkit_docs/C/req/rotation.html
  Notation and axis matrices: its [w]_i rotates coordinates by +w and vectors
  by -w, hence the image's active matrices are [w]_i^T=[-w]_i.

A 3x3 real rotation can act on a three-component ordinary vector or on complex
amplitudes. Using the registered GF3 Fourier basis, A_GFM=F*A*F^dagger is a
complex 3x3 matrix; it preserves the same spectrum and unitarity and acts on
F*v. This is a basis change. Its entries are not GF3 labels, and a real vector's
components need not sum to a normalized probability state.

A separate exact field rotation replaces the real angle by a field parameter u:
  c = (1-u^2)/(1+u^2), s = 2*u/(1+u^2), c^2+s^2 = 1.
Insert c and s in the same axis-matrix pattern. In odd characteristic and when
1+u^2 is nonzero, direct algebra gives R^T R=I and det(R)=1. R(-u) is its inverse.
The separately supported projective parameter infinity supplies c=-1, s=0.
Finite parameters where the denominator vanishes must reject. This construction
does not identify u or infinity with the displayed angle of 232.75 degrees.
It preserves a field quadratic form, not an ordered positive Euclidean norm.

3. ZETA–GAMMA MELLIN IDENTITY
Source: reference/image-equations/HJPJPQbaYAADLiP.jpg
Displayed equation and convergence condition:
  zeta(s)*Gamma(s) = integral_0^infinity t^(s-1)/(exp(t)-1) dt,
  Re(s) > 1.
Visible caption: zeta-Gamma Relation. Portraits supply no mathematical evidence.

Disposition: retained over ordinary complex s in the stated half-plane.
For t>0, t^(s-1) uses the real logarithm. Near zero the integrand behaves as
t^(s-2), requiring Re(s)>1; the large-t tail decays exponentially. Analytic
continuation of zeta or Gamma does not make this unchanged improper integral
converge outside that region. Primary identity:
https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.5.E1
  NIST DLMF equation 25.5.1, multiplied by Gamma(s).

model.zeta limits its numerical ordinary-domain reference to real integer
s=2..8. Any finite cutoff and quadrature are approximations to the integral;
residuals and explicit sampling bounds describe what was actually computed.
The Mellin kernel's sampled values are normalized into a signal, with source
scale and sampling metadata retained. Its finite trace-Fourier spectrum is a
chosen complex data profile, not a predicted quantum wavefunction. It is not
a finite-field zeta or Gamma function and does not inherit the continuum
improper-integral identity.

4. COMMON GFM REAPPLICATION CONTRACT
The established field arithmetic is on GF(q) labels; amplitudes remain complex.
The Fourier convention is F[k,x]=exp(2*pi*i*Tr(k*x)/p)/sqrt(q), positive sign.
Vector profiles use y=F*v and return F^dagger*y plus a round-trip residual.
Operator profiles use A_GFM=F*A*F^dagger with dimension equal to q and return
F^dagger*A_GFM*F plus a residual. These are finite complex linear-algebra laws.
The field-label Fourier definition is grounded in A. Vourdas:
https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0605054

There is no identity-preserving ring homomorphism R -> F_p: it would send p*1
to zero, but 1=p*(1/p) to one, a contradiction. Therefore arbitrary real sine,
cosine, exponential values, irrational constants, continuum integrals and
real derivatives cannot be reduced modulo p without a separate construction.
Integer or rational algebraic models can be transported only with their
denominator and characteristic restrictions. Rational coefficients with a
denominator divisible by p must reject; field operations supply no order.

The applicability manifest accounts for all 20 prior report entries. Entries
without an adapter remain visible as reference material. Rejected expressions,
unspecified modular partial waves, characteristic-two half-phase formulas and
the claimed full-suite audit cannot be made executable by a basis change.
Source images, transcriptions, ordinary reference models, sampled profiles,
complex basis changes and exact field analogues retain distinct domains.

5. PROVENANCE AND VERIFICATION
Original image bytes are retained in reference/image-equations/. SHA-256 and
byte counts appear in image-equations.json and source-register.json. The sole
visible creator label in these images is TheMathFlow on the rotation image;
no further creator, publication date, license or surrounding post text is
inferred. Byte hashes establish identity of retained files, not authorship.
Existing source notices and candidate-report caveats continue to apply.

The local automated verification checks the implemented algebra and numerical
contracts. Live browser rendering, downloads and iframe communication remain
outside that verification unless separately recorded in validation/. No
native quantum hardware, new physics, continuum convergence or universal
finite-field reformulation is established by a successful round trip.
